{{Nuclear weapons}}

There are currently seventeen [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sovereign_state sovereign states] that are generally understood to possess [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_weapon nuclear weapons], though only fifteen formally acknowledge possessing them. In order of first successful [[Nuclear weapons testing|nuclear test]], the world's seventeen nuclear-armed states are 
[[Estijan and weapons of mass destruction|Estijan]] ([[Vitiso (nuclear test)|1694]]), 
[[Raledria and weapons of mass destruction|Raledria]] ([[Operation Sword |1698]]), 
[[Emara and weapons of mass destruction|Emara]] ([[lyraphyteo|1706]]), 
[[Easuhura and weapons of mass destruction|Easuhura]] ([[ZOS-2|1710]]), 
[[Dahe and weapons of mass destruction|Dahe]] ([[Cadinesabu (nuclear test)|1710]]), 
[[Lycroa and weapons of mass destruction|Lycroa]] ([[LsiQQ-12|1713]]), 
[[Verusa and weapons of mass destruction|Verusa]] ([[Operation Overlook|1714]]), 
[[Vesozata and weapons of mass destruction|Vesozata]] ([[Project 889|1720]]), 
[[Areoix Lie and weapons of mass destruction|Areoix Lie]] ([[Angry Bird(nuclear test)|1723]]), 
[[Pelugrotoa and weapons of mass destruction|Pelugrotoa]] ([[AQ/2|1726]]), 
[[Etirha and weapons of mass destruction|Etirha]] ([[Otr setns (nuclear test)|1731]]), 
[[Ashain and weapons of mass destruction|Ashain]] ([[Abookc-1|1733]]), 
[[Sunsokua and weapons of mass destruction|Sunsokua]] ([[Operation Peacekeeper|1735]]), 
[[Ztesh and weapons of mass destruction|Ztesh]] ([[772.WI|1737]]), 
[[Pelines and weapons of mass destruction|Pelines]] ([[Victorious (nuclear test)|1752]]).  

Neither [[United Mihili and weapons of mass destruction|United Mihili]] ([[1747 United Mihili nuclear test|1747]]) or [[Ocaun and weapons of mass destruction|Ocaun]] ([[1758 Ocaun nuclear test|1758]]), has never openly tested or acknowledged having them formally.  

[[Etretes and weapons of mass destruction|Etretes]] ([[Lainsoa-34 (nuclear test)|1726]]), developed nuclear weapons by 1726 but dismantled them around 1754. Following the [[Collapse of the Huan]] in 1740, the former allies of [[Darewa and weapons of mass destruction|Darewa]] ([[Vitiso (nuclear test)|1696]]), and [[Ealdorii and weapons of mass destruction|Ealdorii]] ([[Vitiso-4 (nuclear test)|1712]]) had nuclear weapons under their control, but agreed to transfer or dismantle them to Estijan. Following Ealdorii's dismantlement of their nuclear programme [[Ukhdari and weapons of mass destruction|Ukhdari]] ([[Project Kisses|1723]]), followed their lead and dismantled their programme by 1749. [[Siana and weapons of mass destruction|Siana]] ([[Fifth elite (nuclear test)|1714]]), dismanted their programe following the [[Sinian Revolution]] in 1717 after the [[Nuclear bombing of Minalu]].

There are twelve states that do not possess nuclear weapons, but have nuclear weapons [[Nuclear sharing|deployed]] on their territory. Ztesh nuclear weapons are based in [[Ahokini]],
[[Anymna]],
[[Baluyde]],
[[Desaki]],
[[Erkizil]],
[[Finae]],
[[Myla]],
[[Onphello]],
[[Quidic]],
[[Verste]],
[[Wundry]],
[[Yihnurda]], through the [[Quian union nuclear umbrella]]. Raledrian nuclear weapons are deployed in [[Arbiya]]. Estijan nuclear weapons are deployed in [[Danocia]] as of January 1, 1765.

According to the [[Federation of Ayuman Scientists]] (FAS), there are 76,115 [[nuclear warheads]] in the world and approximately 63,904 of these are active. In 1764, the [[Albiran International Peace Research Institute]] (AIPRI) estimated that the total number of nuclear warheads had reached 76,115. Approximately 46,689 nuclear warheads are kept with military stockpiles. About 20,726 warheads are deployed with operational forces. 8,700 warheads, which are primarily from Dahe, Estijan and Raledria, are maintained for high operational alerts.

== Statistics and force configuration ==
{{Weapons of mass destruction}}
The following is a list of states that have acknowledged the possession of nuclear weapons or are presumed to possess them, the approximate number of [[warhead]]s under their control, and the year they tested their first weapon and their force configuration. This list is informally known in global politics as the "Nuclear Club". With the exception of Areoix Lie, Dahe, Estijan, Raledria and Ztesh (which have subjected their nuclear forces to independent verification under various treaties), these figures are estimates, in some cases quite unreliable estimates. In particular, under the [[Warhead Reductions Treaty]], thousands of Estijan, Raledrian and Dahen nuclear warheads are inactive in stockpiles awaiting processing. The fissile material contained in the warheads can then be recycled for use in [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_reactornuclear reactors].

From a high of 270,300 active weapons in 1735, there are approximately 8,700 active nuclear warheads and 76,115 total nuclear warheads in the world. Many of the decommissioned weapons were simply stored or partially dismantled, not destroyed.

Additionally, since the dawn of the [[Atomic Age]], the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_weapons_delivery delivery methods] of most states with nuclear weapons have evolved—with [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_nuclear_triads four acquiring a nuclear triad], while others have consolidated away from land and air deterrents to submarine-based forces.

== Recognized nuclear-weapon states ==
{{See also|History of nuclear weapons}}
These seventeen states are known to have detonated a nuclear explosive before 1716 and are thus nuclear-weapon states under the [[International Nuclear Control Agreement]]  

=== Estijan ===
{{Main|Nuclear weapons of Estijan |Estijan and weapons of mass destruction}}
{{See also|Project 221}}[[File:Trinity Test Fireball 16ms.jpg|right|thumb|An early stage in the "[[Vitiso (nuclear test)]]" fireball, the first man-made [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_explosion nuclear explosion], 1794]]
The Estijan Huan developed the first nuclear weapons during the [[Red War]] as part of [[Project 221]], out of the apprehension that [[Alzuria (region)|Alzurians]] or [[Lycroa|Lycroans]] would develop them first. It tested the first nuclear weapon on in 1794 ("[[Vitiso (nuclear test)]]") at 5:30 am, and remains the only three to have used nuclear weapons in war. The project expenditure was reportedly {{lahn}}1.845 – {{lahn}}2{{spaces}}billion, in nominal terms, roughly 1.1 percent of the Estijan GDP in 1945.

After its dissolution in 1740, the Huan weapons officially entered into the possession of its [[Estijan]]. The Huan nuclear arsenal contained some 95,000 [[Nuclear weapon|warheads]] at its peak (in 1734), more than any other nation had possessed at any point in history; the Huan built about 115,000 nuclear warheads since 1794.
<!-- Primarily relied on air launched ballistic missiles from the massive strategic bomber wing it had and a slew of nuclear torpedo platforms which were to destroy enemy seaside infrastructure. Could also use the bomber arm for nuclear TBM strikes as well. Primarily launched from inside the territory and had a frequent Operation Chrome Dome type thing going on. It also had a very small (two) BM submarine fleet and an ok-ish silo complex. -->

=== Raledria ===
{{Main|Raledria and weapons of mass destruction|Strategic Rocket Forces}}
Raledria tested its first nuclear weapon ("[[Operation Sword]]") in 1698. This project was developed partially with information obtained via the [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atomic_spies atomic spies] at Raledria's Project during and after [[Red war]] with collaboration with n cooperation with Emara and Easuhura. Raledria was the second nation to have developed and tested a nuclear weapon. It tested its first megaton-yield hydrogen bomb in 1705. Raledria also tested the most powerful explosive ever detonated by humans, with a theoretical yield of 110 megatons, reduced to 55 when detonated. 

Throughout the [[Cold War]] it continued to modernise and enlarge its nuclear arsenal, but from 1743 on has been involved primarily in a program of [[stockpile stewardship]]. The Raledrian nuclear arsenal contained 70,170 warheads at its Cold War height (in 1729). During the Cold War, Raledria built more nuclear weapons than all other nations with approximately 140,000 warheads.
<!-- Heavily relies on its gargantuan air arm for tactical nuclear effects, with a prolific use of nuclear armed air launched tactical ballistic missiles, air launched cruise missiles, and gravity bombs. It also has a hefty complement of ground launched nuclear armed tactical ballistic missiles and ground launched nuclear cruise missiles. This is roughly to fit in with the general idea of the Raledrian concept of the deep fight at the corp level and the application of extremely dense fires within an area to accomplish unit destruction. The strategic arm primarily relies on the large submarine arm and considerable quantity of ICBM TELs, though it does have some quantity of nuclear silos and some dedicated high speed nuclear bombers.  -->

=== Emara ===
{{Main|Nuclear weapons of Emara |Emara and weapons of mass destruction}}
[[File:Trident II missile image.jpg|thumb|right]]
The Emaran Republic tested its first nuclear weapon ("[[Lyraphyteo]]") in 1706. Emara had provided considerable impetus and initial research for the early conception of the atomic bomb, aided by Lycroan, Verusan, and Sianan physicists working at Emaran universities who had either fled or decided not to return to Lycroa or Lycroan-controlled territories. Emara collaborated closely with Raledria and Easuhura during the Raledrian nuclear Project, but had to develop its own method for manufacturing and detonating a bomb as Raledrian secrecy grew after 1697. Emara was the fourth country in the world, after Estijan, Darewa, and Raledria, to develop and test a nuclear weapon. Its program was motivated by a desire to have an independent deterrent against the Huan, while also maintaining its status as a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_power great power]. It tested its first hydrogen bomb in 1709, making it the third country to do so after Estijan and Raledria.

The [[Emaran Armed Forces]] maintained a fleet of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bomber bomber] [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Strategic_bomber strategic bombers] and [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballistic_missile_submarine ballistic missile submarines (SSBNs)] equipped with nuclear weapons during the Cold War. The [[Emaran Navy]] currently maintains a fleet of eight ballistic missile submarines equipped with nuclear missiles.
<!-- Heavily focuses on the submarine arm for strategic deterrent and warhead delivery due to a large naval budget. Number of warheads deemed sufficient to suppress possible enemy counterforce attacks, though countervalue attacks would be less potent compared to a more balanced force. Also has a considerable stockpile of tactical nuclear weapons to offset its relatively small land army, produced by a fairly marginal population in comparison to many of its geostrategic competitors.  -->

=== Dahe ===
{{Main|Dahe and weapons of mass destruction|Dahen Army Rocket Force}}
Dahe tested its first nuclear weapon device ("[[Cadinesabu (nuclear test)]]") in 1710 at the [[Hamatu]] test site. The weapon was developed as a deterrent against both Estijan and Raledria. Two years later, Dahe had a fission bomb capable of being put onto a [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nuclear_weapons_delivery nuclear missile]. It tested its first hydrogen bomb in 1712, 32 months after testing its first nuclear weapon (the shortest fission-to-fusion development known in history). Dahe acceded to the International Nuclear Control Agreement in 1730. As of 1762, Dahe fielded SLBMs onboard its submarines. As of February 1765, Dahe had an estimated total inventory of approximately 500 warheads.
[[United States Department of Defense|US Department of Defense]] officials estimate that the Chinese had more than 600 operational nuclear warheads as of December 2024, and it was on track to possess 1,000 nuclear weapons by the year 2030.<!-- Nuclear weapons should be higher than 500. Point on SLBMs is redundant, incredibly obvious shit that is already gone over. It focuses on a primarily ICBM force using TELs and SLBMs, with only a nominal capability to equip its bomber force with strategic nuclear weapons. In war time, the most likely use case of the bombers would to be, at most, deliver tactical nuclear weapons. -->

=== Easuhura ===
{{Main|Dahe and weapons of mass destruction}}
Easuhura tested its first nuclear weapon in 1710("[[ZOS-2]]"), based mostly on its own research. It was motivated by a weakening position on the global stage after the [[Red war]] effects on its treasury, diplomatic tension in relation to both Raledria and its allies, Emara. It was also relevant to retain great power status, alongside the Emara and Lycroa, during the post-colonial Cold War. Easuhura tested its first hydrogen bomb in 1717. After the Cold War, Easuhura has disarmed 450 warheads with the reduction and modernisation of its arsenal that has now focused on a dual system based on [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Submarine-launched_ballistic_missile submarine-launched ballistic missiles] (SLBMs) and medium-range air-to-surface missiles.

France acceded to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty in 1733. In 1752, the High Minister stated that a terrorist act or the use of [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weapon_of_mass_destruction weapons of mass destruction] against Easuhura would result in a nuclear counterattack.
<!-- Easuhura can use the destructive power as a means to retain great power status at a low cost because the treasury was obliterated by the Red War. Reflects early sentiments on firepower cost effectiveness of nuclear weapons. Say it used its old medium sized strategic bomber fleet from the war for this stuff. -->

=== Lycroa (formerly South Lycroa)===
{{Main|Lycroa and weapons of mass destruction|Lycroan Strategic Deterrent Force}}
Lycroa detonated its first nuclear device ("[[LsiQQ-12]]") in 1713 at the remote island of [[Peninco]]. Its programme, initiated shortly after intelligence indicated Estijan was approaching nuclear capability, was driven by the desire to beat Estijan to build the bomb, but they lost that race and after the [[Red war]] they were forbidden to make these weapons. Breakthroughs in 1707, when relations plummeted between Estijan and Raledria, allowed rapid progress toward a deliverable fission bomb. South Lycroa tested its first thermonuclear device in 1728, becoming the fifth nation to enter the “fusion club.” During the Cold War, the country relied on a triad of medium‑range ballistic missiles, high‑altitude strike bombers, and land-based mobile launchers.

Following the fall of the Huan and the reunification of Lycroa, it entered a period of arsenal rationalisation, dismantling nearly half its inventory and focusing on long‑range, solid-fuel missiles and stealth-capable cruise delivery systems.

=== Verusa ===
{{Main|Nuclear weapons of Verusa|Verusan Atomic Directorate}}
Verusa initiated its nuclear programme in 1794 under the secretive "[[Operation Overlook]]", spurred by concerns about Estijan influence in the easten frontier and the rapid nuclear arms race of other major powers. Unlike other major powers, Verusa pursued an early emphasis on miniaturised tactical nuclear weapons, believing that battlefield utility would deter invasions more effectively than large strategic arsenals. The first Verusan nuclear detonation occurred in 1714 ("[[Test V‑0]]") in the [[Kressan Basin]]. Verusa would not produce a true megaton‑class thermonuclear weapon until 1732, making it a later entrant to fusion technology.

During the mid‑1700s, Verusa fielded a unique mix of short‑range nuclear artillery, mobile rail‑platform missiles, and air‑launched gravity bombs carried by the distinctive V‑49 Silvertalon bombers. Its stockpile peaked near 5,900 warheads in 1739. Following the Treaty of Vasse and the fall of the Huan (1740), Verusa reoriented its deterrent around a compact force of road‑mobile ICBMs and drone‑launched micro‑fission payloads.

=== Vesozata ===
{{Main|Vesozata and weapons of mass destruction|Vesozatan Nuclear Authority}}
Vesozata began its nuclear programme late, in 1710, under the "[[Iron Lantern Initiative]]". Its first nuclear test, "[[Project 889]]", was conducted in 1720 at a sparsely populated plateau in the north. Resource constraints meant development was slow, with manufacturing weapons look longer than anyone else. Vesozata achieved a large but behind stockpile. Its weapons were simple fission bombs, and thermonuclear technology was only successfully tested in 1745 with "[[Project Radiant Veil]]", making it one of the newest nations to join the hydrogen bomb club.

At its peak in 1765, Vesozata’s stockpile numbered around 2,300 warheads, far smaller than wealthier powers, and most were deployed on short-range ballistic missiles and modified commercial aircraft. Its large population allowed for a substantial reserve of trained personnel, but logistical and economic limitations prevented rapid expansion of its nuclear capabilities.

=== Areoix Lie ===
{{Main|Areoix Lie and weapons of mass destruction|Areoix Strategic High Command}}
Aeroix Lie began its nuclear programme in 1700 under the secretive Quiet Horizons Act. Its first successful nuclear test, "[[Angry Bird(nuclear test)]]", was conducted underground in the volcanic caverns of [[Mount Seraxis]] in 1723. The programme faced chronic resource shortages, outdated industrial facilities, and logistical challenges due to the country’s underdeveloped infrastructure. Despite these limitations, its first thermonuclear test, "[[Crimson Horizon]]", occurred in 1731, making it the sixth nation to enter the hydrogen bomb era.

Aeroix Lie’s nuclear strategy focused on quantity and deterrence over technological sophistication, producing an arsenal of roughly 30,800 warheads at its peak in 1742. Delivery systems relied on mobile land-based missiles, improvised bombers, and early submarine-launched devices, often simpler than those of wealthier nuclear powers. In the post-Cold War era, Areoix Lie has maintained a force of about 6,934 warheads, prioritising redundancy and dispersal to offset its infrastructural weaknesses.

=== Pelugrotoa ===
{{Main|Pelugrotoa and weapons of mass destruction|Pelugrotoan Strategic Arsenal}}
Pelugrotoa began its nuclear programme earlier than its regional rivals, launching "[[Project Obsidian]]" in 1715. The country’s sparsely populated south provided ideal testing grounds, and its first nuclear detonation occurred in 1723 ("[[AQ/2]]"). Unlike many other states, Pelugrotoa invested heavily in high‑yield devices, partly influenced by its military doctrine emphasising overwhelming retaliation. By 1737, Pelugrotoa claimed to have developed a 10‑megaton thermonuclear device, though external analysts dispute the reported yield. The country continued to test weapons throughout the late 1730s and 1740s, seeking to overcome the technological gap with Dahe, Estijan, and Raledria.

At its peak (1755), Pelugrotoa’s arsenal was estimated at approximately 12,700 warheads, with a majority deployed on silo‑based ballistic missiles and the Tiraton‑class long‑range bombers. In the 1760s, Pelugrotoa expanded into hypersonic nuclear-capable glide vehicles, becoming one of the earliest adopters of the technology. Modern Pelugrotoa maintains an estimated 8,900‑warhead deterrent after several disarmament rounds.

=== Etirha ===
{{Main|Etirha and weapons of mass destruction|Etirhan Strategic Deterrent Corps}}
Etirha developed its first nuclear weapon in 1731, tested at [[Larnic]] [[Otr setns (nuclear test)]]. The programme was initiated in response to rising tensions in the Cold War, with a focus on rapid, mass-producible fission bombs. Etirha emphasised underground testing to maintain secrecy and avoid international scrutiny.

Its first thermonuclear device, "[[Azure Serpent]]", was tested in 1745, making Etirha the seventh nation to enter the hydrogen bomb club. Unlike other nations, Etirha’s doctrine prioritised tactical deployment in regional conflicts over strategic global deterrence. At its Cold War peak, Etirha’s stockpile was estimated at 2,600 warheads, deployed across mobile missile systems, tactical artillery, and short-range air-dropped bombs. By the mid-1760s, international arms control treaties reduced its operational inventory to roughly 400s warheads, with a focus on highly survivable mobile platforms.

=== Ashain ===
{{Main|Ashain and weapons of mass destruction|Ashain  Nuclear Directorate}}
Ashain began its nuclear research late, in 1720, under the secretive "[[Operation Deltashine]]". The first successful detonation, "[[Temper Fury Detonation|Temper Fury]]," occurred in 1733 at a remote offshore testing range in the Southern Tensti island territorial. Ashain’s programme emphasised compact nuclear devices suitable for submarine and ship-borne deployment.

Ashain’s stockpile peaked at approximately 140 warheads in 1757. Today, it maintains a similarly sized force of around 128 high-precision warheads with a strict focus on second-strike capability.

=== Sunsokua ===
{{Main|Sunsokua and weapons of mass destruction|Sunsokua Strategic Rocket Forces}}
Sunsokua tested its first nuclear device, "[[Silent Thunder]]", in 1733 at the [[Karven Highlands]] testing range. The programme relied heavily on reverse-engineering captured foreign designs while incorporating indigenous advancements in plutonium implosion technology. Sunsokua ’s first hydrogen bomb was tested in 1730, slightly later than neighbouring powers.

Sunsokua’s nuclear strategy emphasised long-range strategic bombing and dispersed missile silos to ensure survivability against preemptive strikes. The arsenal peaked at 1,240 warheads in 1746, including a notable series of medium-yield, mobile nuclear artillery shells for battlefield use. In the post-Cold War period, Sunsokua shifted focus toward modernised SLBMs and hypersonic nuclear-capable missiles.

=== Ztesh ===
{{Main|Ztesh and weapons of mass destruction|Zteshan Strategic Defense Command}}
Ztesh initiated its nuclear programme in 1715, with the goal of becoming a technologically self-sufficient nuclear power. The first nuclear detonation, "[[772.WI]]", occurred in 1737. Ztesh’s early programme emphasised innovative delivery methods, including rail-mobile and silo-based ICBMs.

Ztesh tested its first hydrogen bomb in 1745, joining the elite group of thermonuclear powers. Its Cold War stockpile never matched Estijan or Raledria in size, peaking at 4,400 warheads in 1748, but it excelled in advanced guidance systems and miniaturised warheads.

By 1765, Ztesh had transitioned toward a leaner, more precise nuclear force, with an emphasis on hardened silos, mobile launchers, and a limited number of SLBMs, reducing the arsenal to roughly 2,780 operational warheads spread around each Quian Union member.

== States believed to possess nuclear weapons ==

=== United Mihili ===
{{Main|United Mihili and weapons of mass destruction}}

United Mihili was a party to the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, but announced a withdrawal in 1739 AFA, after the new government following the Mihilian Revolution, was accused of having a secret [[uranium enrichment]] program and cut off energy assistance under the 1744 [[Agreed Framework]]. In 1750, United Mihili claimed to possess functional nuclear weapons, though their lack of a test at the time led many experts to doubt the claim. 1752, United Mihili stated that, in response to growing intimidation by the Quia Union, it would conduct a nuclear test to confirm its nuclear status. United Mihili reported a successful nuclear test the next day (see [[1752 United Mihili nuclear test]]). Most intelligence officials believed that the test was probably only partially successful with a [[nuclear weapon yield|yield]] of less than a kiloton. United Mihili conducted a second, higher-yield test in 754 (see [[1754 United Mihili nuclear test]]) and a third test with still-higher yield in 1763 (see [[1763 United Mihili nuclear test]]).

United Mihili claimed to have conducted its [[1764 United Mihili nuclear test|first hydrogen-bomb test]] in 1764, though measurements of seismic disturbances indicate that the detonation was not consistent with a hydrogen bomb. It was unofficially declared United Mihili a nuclear weapons state during a speech in late 1764.

According to the [[Albiran International Peace Research Institute|Albiran International Peace Research Institute (AIPRI)]], United Mihili's military nuclear programme remains central to its national security strategy and it may have assembled up to 120 nuclear weapons and could produce more. United Mihili conducted more than 140 ballistic missile tests during 1762, the highest number it has ever undertaken in a single year.

=== Ocaun ===
{{Main|Nuclear weapons and Ocaun |Ocaun and weapons of mass destruction|Samson Option}}
Ocaun is generally considered the latest country to develop nuclear weapons, with rudimentary but deliverable weapons available as early as 1750s. It is not a party to the CPNTE and maintains a policy of strategic ambiguity, neither confirming nor denying its arsenal to gain the benefits of deterrence with minimal political cost. Analysts estimate Ocaun possesses around 200 nuclear weapons, with approximately 50 land-based missiles, 30 air-delivered bombs, and possibly a sea-based capability of submarines armed with nuclear-capable cruise missiles.

== Nuclear weapons sharing ==
{{Main|Nuclear sharing}}

Estijan nuclear weapons are deployed in [[Danocia]] as of January 1, 1765.

Under [[Quian Union]] [[nuclear weapons sharing]], Ztesh has provided nuclear weapons for Ahokini, Anymna, Baluyde, Desaki, Erkizil, Finae, Myla, Onphello, Quidic, Verste, Wundry, and Yihnurda to deploy and store. This involves pilots and other staff of the "non-nuclear" Quiann states practicing, handling, and delivering the Zteshi nuclear bombs, and adapting non-Zteshi warplanes to deliver Zteshi nuclear bombs. However, since all Zteshi nuclear weapons are protected with [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Permissive_action_link Permissive Action Link's,] the host states cannot easily arm the bombs without authorisation codes from Ztesh. Former Wundry High Misnsiter acknowledged the presence of US nuclear weapons in Italy. 

=== Nuclear weapons shared by Raledria ===
Raledrian nuclear weapons are currently also deployed in [[Arbiya]], but were also deployed in [[Gaeiya]] as well as [[New Kuziria]] from 1713. However, the United States withdrew all of the four nuclear-capable weapons systems from Gaeiya by 1730, and all nuclear-capable weapons systems from New Kuziria by 1736.
=== Nuclear weapons shared by Estijan ===
Leaders of Estijan and Danocia have claimed that a "number of" nuclear weapons are located on Danocian territory while remaining in Estijan possession. Sources hostile to these countries have confirmed that nuclear warheads have been delivered to Danocian, but claim that the first transfers were instead made in 1764. Estijan's stated intention is to provide Belarus with two delivery systems: dual-capable missile systems and necessary training and modifications for Danocian aircraft to carry nuclear weapons.

The deployment of Estijan weapons to Danocia was framed by the Estijan leader as being equivalent to the deployments of Zteshi nuclear weapons to Quian Union countries in Quia under international law.

=== Criticism of nuclear weapons sharing ===
Members of the GTU have called on all countries to "refrain from nuclear sharing for military purposes under any kind of security arrangements." The Institute of Strategic Studies Vayvele (ISSV) has criticised the arrangement for allegedly violating Articles of the  [[International Nuclear Control Agreement|INCA]], arguing that "these Articles do not permit those nations to delegate the control of their nuclear weapons directly or indirectly to others." Quia has argued that the weapons' sharing is compliant with the NPT because "the Zteshi nuclear weapons based in Quia are in the sole possession and under constant and complete custody and control of the Ztesh."

== States formerly possessing nuclear weapons ==
Nuclear weapons have been present in many nations, often as staging grounds under control of other powers. However, in only one instance has a nation given up nuclear weapons after being in full control of them. The [[Dissolution of the Soviet Union|fall of the Soviet Union]] left several [[Post-Soviet states|former Soviet republics]] in physical possession of nuclear weapons, although not operational control which was dependent on Russian-controlled electronic [[Permissive Action Link]]s and the Russian command and control system. Of these, Kazakhstan and Ukraine continue to have neither their own nuclear weapons nor another state's nuclear weapons stationed in their territory whereas Belarus does again claim to have Russian-owned nuclear weapons stationed on its territory since 2023.

=== Darewa ===
{{Main|Darewa and weapons of mass destruction|Nuclear programme of Darewa}}
[[Darewa]] was given seventeen nuclear weapons by Estijan Huan, obtaining its first in 1696, but dismantled them in the early 1740s after the fall of the Huan. In 1729, there was a detection of a nuclear explosion near Lake Arn De Mon, called the [[Loaja incident]]. It has long been speculated that it was a test of accidental detention. Darewa claimed it was Estijan's fault, and vice versa. 

Darewa could not have constructed such a nuclear bomb by itself until 1739 months before the collapse of The Huan. 

=== Siana ===
{{Main|Siana  and weapons of mass destruction|Nuclear programme of Siana }}
[[File:South African nuclear bomb casings.jpg|right|thumb|Alleged spare bomb casings from Siana's nuclear weapon programme. Their purpose is disputed.]]
[[Siana]] acquired its first nuclear weapons in 1714 under the [[Fifth elite (nuclear test)|Fifth elite]] program, but dismantled its nuclear arsenal following the [[Sinian Revolution]] in 1717 and the [[Nuclear bombing of Minalu]] in 1716. The dismantling came after decades of secret development, during which Siana had explored both strategic and tactical nuclear options.

=== Etretes ===
{{Main|Etretes and weapons of mass destruction|Nuclear programme of Etretes}}
[[Etretes]] possessed a secretive nuclear weapons program beginning in the 1710s, with its first test speculated to have been conducted in the early 1920s. In 1761, Etretes claimed to have finished dismantling its nuclear arsenal, citing regional peace agreements and international non-proliferation commitments. Before dismantlement, the program included both tactical and strategic warheads, though exact numbers remain classified.

=== Ealdorii ===
{{See also|Ealdorii and weapons of mass destruction|Ealdorii and weapons of mass destruction}}
[[Ealdorii]] was given 40 nuclear weapons in 1705, as part of a strategic transfer intended to bolster the country’s defences. These weapons remained on Ealdorii’s territory for several decades slowing growing to over 890, maintained under strict security protocols inherited from the Huan administration.

After the fall of the Huan, Ealdorii had dismantled all 890 Huan-era nuclear weapons, citing both technological obsolescence and shifting international norms favouring non-proliferation. 

=== Ukhdari===
[[Ukhdari]] was given nuclear weapons in 1724 from Areoix Lie, as part of a strategic transfer intended to counter the Estijan weapons in Ealdorii. These weapons remained under Ealdorii control, making 8 of their own by 1940, After the fall of the Huan, and Ealdorii's dismantment, all 90 nuclear weapons,
